items.summary: Since B. R. Ambedkar converted in 1956, Buddhism has become a central reference point in debates about caste and Brahminical dominance. How did a religion that began in antiquity grow into a modern political and intellectual movement? In the first episode of Seeking Sangha, a special focus series on What's Your ISM?, The News Minute Executive Editor Sudipto Mondal speaks to historian and author Douglas Ober about his book Dust on the Throne and the rediscovery of Buddhism in British colonial times. They discuss Buddhist modernity, Ambedkar’s engagement with Buddhism, the relationship between Buddhism and Brahmanism, and how European scholarship cast new light on the way India’s Buddhist past was understood. Sudipto and Douglas trace the Buddhist revival in the 19th and 20th centuries through figures such as Anagarika Dharmapala, Kripa Saran, and Iyothee Thass who came before Ambedkar and examine Buddhism’s relationship with caste and anti-caste politics. They also discuss Ambedkar, JK Birla, and Gandhi’s approaches to Buddhism, before looking at how Nehru and Modi have used Buddhism as cultural diplomacy and soft power. Like Sudipto’s Ism show? items.title: Supreme Court pulls up Centre over "unannounced" motor accident victim compensation scheme
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed disapproval over the Central government’s quiet rollout of a critical welfare measure for motor accident victims, terming the newly framed Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026 an "unannounced law." A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan observed that beneficial social legislation is rendered meaningless if the general public remains completely unaware of its existence. “This is an unannounced law. People should know because it’s a beneficial piece of legislation. Common man would not come to know,” the Bench remarked, directing the Union government to launch a widespread publicity campaign to inform citizens of their rights under the new rules. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Viswanathan The issue arose during a contempt petition alleging non-compliance with an April 28, 2025 order. The Court had previously directed the Centre to establish a statutory mechanism under Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act to ensure swift interim financial relief to road accident victims and their families. During today's hearing, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Vikramjit Banerjee informed the Court that the Central government had indeed framed the scheme, titled the Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026 . Drawing attention to Clause 6, the ASG submitted that a letter had already been dispatched on February 23 to Chief Secretaries of all States to circulate the new guidelines. However, the revelation caught both the applicant (appearing in person) and the amicus curiae entirely by surprise, as neither had any prior knowledge that the scheme had already been framed and dispatched. Beyond the lack of publicity, the amicus curiae and the applicant also flagged that the new scheme applies exclusively to insured motor vehicles where the insurance company disburses compensation. They pointed out that the scheme leaves victims of uninsured motor vehicles unprotected, where the driver or owner of the vehicle is directly liable to pay damages. items.title: Supreme Court stays demolition of CSI church in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed a Madras High Court order directing the demolition of a Christian CSI church at Thippanampatti village of Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district [ Tirunelveli Diocesan Trust Association v. The District Collector ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath , R Mahadevan , and Aparesh Kumar Singh also sought the response of the Tamil Nadu government and other respondents on a Special Leave Petition (SLP) challenging the High Court's October 1 judgment. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The case concerned a building that has been used for prayer services by members of the Church of South India (CSI) in Thippanampatti village since 2016. Earlier, a church built around 1972 was being used for prayer services. However, since the old church was too small to accommodate all church-going members, a decision was taken to shift to a new church. In 2014, a CSI Trust purchased 10 cents of land and got permission to use the property to build a CSI community hall. In 2016, a church spire was added to the building and the premises began to be used as a church. However, in June 2016, a local resident named Balakrishna Prabhu moved a plea before the Madras High Court urging it to direct the District Collector to consider his representation seeking a restraint on the construction and operation of the building as a church. During these proceedings, the State informed the Court that no application was made to use the building as a church. In response, the Diocese's counsel agreed to submit an application seeking such permission. The District Collector later rejected the Diocese's plea for permission to continue using the premises as a church citing potential law and order concerns. On October 1, the Madras High Court dismissed the Diocese's challenge to the District Collector's order and directed that the church spire be pulled down and the building be restored to a community hall. The High Court accepted the State's justification for the District Collector's order, including concerns that there appeared to be a "rift between two religious groups." The Tirunelveli Diocesan Trust Association has now approached the Supreme Court challenging this ruling. items.title: Delhi High Court refuses to stay probe against journalists in SC/ST Act case filed by ACP Vivek Bhagat
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to stay the investigation into the criminal case filed against a woman journalist for allegedly making casteist remarks against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat during a protest in the national capital on October 3. A request to stay the investigation was made before Justice Mini Pushkarna during the hearing of a plea moved by the journalist for quashing the FIR. Senior Advocate Tanveer Ahmed Mir appearing for the journalist and one other accused requested for an order restraining the police from taking further steps in relation to the investigation in this case. He said that ACP Bhagat's SC/ST Act case was a counterblast to a sexual harassment complaint filed by the woman journalist against him. "I cannot pass such an order [staying investigation]," Justice Pushkarna said. The Court said the case will be heard immediately after the Dussehra break. Justice Mini Pushkarna The Delhi Police had registered the FIR against the woman journalist and one Gajendra Singh, associated with a news portal, as well as an unidentified person, on a complaint filed by ACP Bhagat over alleged casteist remarks during a protest in Delhi on October 3. According to reports, the FIR was registered at Parliament Street police station on October 13 under provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 221, 356(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Bhagat alleged that the journalist made derogatory remarks about his caste and questioned his appointment as an ACP while he was performing law-and-order duties near Jantar Mantar. The case comes amid a separate complaint by the journalist accusing Bhagat of sexual harassment and manhandling during the same protest. On Thursday, the Supreme Court restrained the Delhi Police from taking any coercive action against the journalist in the case registered under the provisions of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

items.title: Lucio AI launches Legal Research Agent in Open Beta, offers 25 Free Searches
items.summary: Lucio AI has launched Lucio Research , a legal research agent released as an open beta through Lucio Labs. The tool searches, screens, reads and cites across hundreds of legal sources for each question. It is free to use for one month, with up to 25 searches per user. The launch addresses a familiar constraint in legal research. Much of the time spent on a research question goes into finding and screening material rather than analysing it and research usually ends when time runs out rather than when every relevant authority has been read. Lucio says the beta is designed to test how far that limit can be pushed. Lucio Research runs in two modes. According to the company, Standard mode runs a focused search of the core authorities and typically reviews 300 to 500 sources per question. In-depth mode explores about three times as many sources and checks for gaps, usually returning an answer in under three minutes. The company says it often reviews 800 to 1,500 sources in this mode and more than 2,000 on some questions. Lucio says that, in its testing, public AI models usually review far fewer sources and that a deep research query on ChatGPT takes around 10 minutes. Each answer cites its authorities inline. A separate view lists every source the tool considered, sorted into highly relevant, relevant, flagged and discarded, so a lawyer can see what was set aside as well as what was relied on. Lucio attributes the speed to its architecture rather than to reading less. In place of a pure agent loop, in which a model takes one step at a time, the system uses fast decision models and an architecture built to maximise parallel work. The company says the tool is optimised for case law research across the US, the UK and India and that its analysis of regulation and legislation is still being improved. Darsan Guruvayurappan , Co-Founder, Lucio AI, added, "The engineering problem is that breadth usually costs time. items.title: Karnataka High Court directs State to set up district-level committees to tackle illegal immigration
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday directed the State government to establish district-level committees to deal with illegal immigration within three months [Nagendrappa T & others v. Justice M Nagaprasanna issued the direction while disposing of a petition filed by Bengaluru resident Nagendrappa T, who had challenged his arrest after complaining about illegal immigrants in the city. “The said committee shall be put in place within three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and compliance to that effect be placed before the Registry of this Court in the subject petition,” the Court directed. Justice M Nagaprasanna The Court also quashed the FIRs registered against him by the Bellandur and Varthur police. “The criminal petitions are allowed. On July 29, the High Court had come down heavily on the State police and the Home Department while staying the criminal proceedings against Nagendrappa . “Ask them to control this (illegal immigration), leave other talks. [Boddu Reddy v. Union of India] A coram of Judicial Member Justice (retired) Pushpa Sathyanarayana and Expert Member Prashant Gargava posted the matter for further hearing on October 26. items.title: Calcutta High Court stays order allowing CPI(M) to set up book stall near its office
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday stayed a single-judge's order allowing erection of a temporary book stall by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] near its party office at the Bongaon Jessore Road. A bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Shabbar Rashidi passed the order on an appeal by the State government. The government had challenged the order passed by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya on Thursday on a petition moved by the CPI(M). The party had alleged that the State was preventing from installing the stall Advocate Shamim Ahammed, representing the CPI(M) pointed out that many people had erected their stalls in the same locality but it was only the CPI(M) members who were being obstructed. He further said that many of these stalls were being operated without proper approval. To this, the Chief Justice said, "Can there be any justification?...Just because many thieves are roaming around, I [CPI(M)] will not be caught?" CPI(M) also said that it is their fundamental duty to disseminate knowledge and information through literature and books. Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharyya , appearing for the State said that the CPI(M) members were encroaching public land by erecting their stall and could not prefer a petition to uphold their fundamental rights in the case. He said that the CPI(M) members had suppressed certain documents before the single-judge. "It is the responsibility of police officials to prevent public nuisance," the State counsel said. Considering the arguments, the division bench stayed the operation of the CPI(M) book stall during the remaining Durga Puja days. Meanwhile, the Court took note of a statement that a group namely Hindu Jagran Manch (HJM) has erected their own stall in the place where the CPI(M) book stall was to be set up. The Court directed the State to check whether they have any approval for it and take appropriate steps in case of any violation. The matter will be heard next on January 21, 2027.

items.title: Madras High Court allows RSS marches across 128 locations, criticises TN Police
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Friday permitted the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to conduct route marches across Tamil Nadu on October 25 and November 1, while criticising the State police for repeatedly denying permission. [Jagadeesan v. State] Justice V Lakshminarayanan observed that despite several orders of the High Court and Supreme Court, the Tamil Nadu Police had consistently relied on the same reasons to deny permission for the processions. " One thing must be said to the credit of the Tamil Nadu police. They have not come up with any novel reasons for rejection. They have consistently given the very reasons which this Court found as lame ," the judge remarked. The Court also directed the police not to prolong the matter and to coordinate with RSS organisers to finalise the timings and locations of the marches and subsequent public meetings by Monday, October 19. Justice V Lakshminarayanan The case arose from an application submitted by the RSS State Secretary on October 3 seeking permission to conduct route marches and public meetings as part of the organisation's Vijayadashami celebrations. The RSS had proposed October 18, October 25 and November 1 as alternative dates for the processions. However, police authorities rejected applications citing the presence of places of worship belonging to other communities along the proposed routes, statues of rationalist leaders, traffic congestion, use of loudspeakers and possible law and order problems. Justice Lakshminarayanan noted that these grounds had already been considered and disapproved in earlier proceedings involving the RSS. Tracing the litigation to 2022, the Court referred to several earlier decisions recognising the organisation's right to conduct route marches, subject to lawful restrictions. It also referred to a 2023 ruling holding that public roads are secular spaces accessible to everyone irrespective of religion, caste or creed. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes FIR against Amit Malviya over X post on Rahul Gandhi
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday quashed a First Information Report (FIR) registered against former BJP IT Cell convenor Amit Malviya over a social media post criticising Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and his remarks on Operation Sindoor. Justice M Nagaprasanna today allowed a petition filed by Malviya to quash the case. Justice M Nagaprasanna Malviya had challenged an FIR registered against him citing the offences under Sections 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause a riot) and 353 (public mischief) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) The case concerned a post made by Malviya on X (formerly Twitter) on May 20, 2025. Malviya published the image of a face in the post, half of which was that of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, with the other half being that of Pakistani Army chief Asim Munir. The post criticised Rahul Gandhi's remarks on Operation Sindoor - India's cross-border military response to Pakistan afte the Pahalgam terror attack. Malviya accused the Congress leader of speaking the language of Pakistan and its beneficiaries. The post further questioned why Rahul Gandhi had not congratulated the Prime Minister of India over Operation Sindoor, and whether the Congress leader was aiming for Nishan-e-Pakistan, the highest civilian honour conferred in Pakistan. A complaint was filed by Congress functionary Sridhar MM against Malviya over this post. Sridhar alleged that the post was false, malicious and provocative and had the potential to incite hostility towards Gandhi and the Congress party. Based on the complaint, the police registered the FIR on May 20, 2025. Malviya challenged this FIR before the High Court. He argued that his post constituted political speech and criticism on a matter of public interest. He contended that the criminal proceedings against him amounted to an abuse of the process of law. On May 22, 2025, Justice S Rachiah stayed the case after noting that prima facie, the allegations against Malviya did not attract the offence under Section 352 of the BNS. Today, the Court proceeded to allow Malviya's plea and quashed the case altogether. Senior Advocate M Aruna Shyam and advocate Suyog Herele E appeared for Malviya. Senior Advocate M Aruna Shyam State Public Prosecutor B N Jagadesh appeared for State. Advocate BN Jagadeesh Detailed order is awaited.

His stellar academic record laid the foundation for a distinguished career: after graduating in Science with distinction in 1974, Trivedi topped Gujarat University in his LL.B. in 1977. Concurrently, he secured a Master’s degree in Personnel Management & Labour Welfare. He joined the Bar in 1977 while also teaching at the Sir LA Shah Law College, MN Law College and the Institute of Company Secretaries as visiting faculty. items.title: Twisha Sharma death: Supreme Court stays trial, orders expeditious decision on bail pleas of accused
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed the trial proceedings in the alleged dowry death case of Twisha Sharma, a woman who was married to a lawyer in Bhopal. A bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi passed the order while issuing notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on a petition moved by the victim's father for transfer of the trial to Delhi. "While trial proceedings on merits shall remain stayed, the bail applications filed by respondent 2 and 3 to be decided within two weeks," the Court ordered. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Noida-based Twisha Sharma had married Bhopal-based lawyer Samarth Singh after the two met through a dating app. Barely five months into the marriage, Sharma was found hanging at her matrimonial home in Bhopal on May 12. Her family accused her husband and in-laws of subjecting her to persistent domestic violence and harassment over dowry demands, leading to the registration of an FIR at Katara Hills police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Dowry Prohibition Act. Twisha’s mother-in-law, Giribala Singh, former President of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Madhya Pradesh, was soon granted anticipatory bail by a sessions court. The Madhya Pradesh High Court later cancelled the relief after the State government and the victim's family challenged the order. Twisha Sharma death: MP High Court cancels anticipatory bail of mother-in-law Giribala Singh The High Court then also ordered a second post-mortem of Sharma’s body by a team of doctors from AIIMS Delhi after her family sought a fresh examination to ascertain the exact cause of death. The CBI later arrested Giribala Singh and Samarth Singh. After their period of CBI custody ended on June 2, a Bhopal court remanded both accused to judicial custody. Their bail petitions are currently pending. Senior Advocates Siddharth Agarwal and Siddharth Luthra appeared for the petitioner. Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave represented the accused.

items.title: JGLS team wins 2nd CCI-MNLUCS National Antitrust Moot Court Competition

It was held in collaboration with the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and Phoenix Legal. This edition saw participation from 78 teams from law schools and universities across India. Because of the higher participation, a Memorial Selection Round was introduced, after which 32 teams were shortlisted for the preliminary rounds. The moot proposition dealt with competition law in the digital economy. Teams had to argue questions of statutory interpretation, competition policy and enforcement. The competition opened with an online inauguration on September 11. Avaantika Kakkar , Partner and Head of Competition Law at Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, was the chief guest. The 4 semi-finalists were National Law Institute University (NLIU), Bhopal; JGLS; National Forensic Sciences University, Delhi; and Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies, Delhi. The final was judged by Neha Raj Kochhar , Director (Law), CCI; Kunal Mehra , Senior Partner, Phoenix Legal; and Akshay Nanda , Partner, Saraf and Partners. The semi-finals were judged by Amit Tayal , Joint Director (Law), CCI; Arvind Kumar Anand , Joint Director (Economics), CCI; Sumeet Singh , Chief Legal Officer, BharatPe; and Danish Khan , Associate Partner, Phoenix Legal. At the valedictory ceremony, Justice VK Jadhav , former Bombay High Court judge and Vice Chairman of the Maharashtra Administrative Tribunal, was the chief guest. Kochhar was the guest of honour. items.title: Using children for election campaign in bad taste but not ground to invalidate election: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Thursday held that the use of children for a political party's election campaigns is in bad taste, but such conduct, by itself, is not a ground to invalidate an election [ K Sivakumar v R Rajendran ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy criticised the use of children to influence their parents' voting choices through social media videos. However, the Court held that such persuasion could not automatically be treated as undue influence under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RP Act), to void an election. The Court added that it is up to lawmakers in Parliament to decide whether such practices should be banned or made a ground for setting aside an election. " The entire act of involving tender children is in bad taste, and the tasks they were allowed to perform reflect poor parenting; making reels out of it is cheap and politically motivated. This is a larger debate for the nation and Parliament to consider, including whether to prohibit it or make it grounds to set aside the election," the Court held. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy Madras High Court Involving tender children is in bad taste... reflect poor parenting; making reels out of it is cheap and politically motivated. This is a larger debate for Parliament to consider. The Court made the observation while rejecting an election petition challenging the victory of Tamizhaga Vetri Kazhagam (TVK) candidate R Rajendran from the Salem North Assembly constituency in the 2026 Tamil Nadu elections. The petition was filed by DMK candidate Sivakumar, who had lost to Rajendran by 14,034 votes. Sivakumar argued that Rajendran's election was marred by undue influence. He contended that TVK had used children in election campaigns in violation of Election Commission guidelines prohibiting their involvement in election-related activities. He also relied on a speech delivered by TVK president Joseph Vijay (now Chief Minister) on April 21, 2026, in which the actor-politician allegedly urged children to pester their parents to vote for TVK, just as they would demand chocolates such as Kinder Joy. The petition also cited several social media videos purportedly showing children pressuring or threatening family members to secure votes for TVK. These included a child threatening to throw cow dung at a parent, another threatening suicide and a young woman allegedly threatening to poison her father's food if he refused to vote for the party. items.title: Actor Imran Khan to move Bombay High Court against notice to leave India after protests against CEC
items.summary: Bollywood actor Imran Khan will approach the Bombay High Court challenging the notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) which directs him to leave the country by October 28 for allegedly violating the Foreigners Act. Once the plea is filed, it will be moved for an urgent hearing. The plea is likely to be heard by the division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna . Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna Khan is being represented by advocates Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Chirag Naik from MZM Legal LLP. The administrative action follows Khan’s detention on October 10 during a demonstration at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. After the demonstration, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kirit Somaiya lodged a complaint at the Gamdevi police station. He alleged that the actor, a United States (US) citizen, breached the Foreigners Act by participating in the political morcha. The Gamdevi police subsequently forwarded the complaint to the FRRO for necessary action. The immigration authority acted on the complaint and served an expulsion notice to the actor. According to reports , the FRRO directive cited his US citizenship and flagged his participation in the demonstration as an infraction of immigration and foreigners regulations. Khan has been ordered to leave the territory of India on or before October 28. Khan is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder. While the 2005 OCI scheme grants foreign nationals of Indian origin a lifelong visa to visit and reside in India, it does not confer Indian citizenship or political privileges such as voting or contesting elections. Under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the Central government has the authority to direct a foreigner to “not remain in India or in any specified area therein". Justice Vinod Kumar also refused to accept managing director Ajay Singh's Gurgaon property as security since SpiceJet failed to deposit ₹50 crores with the Registrar General of the Court in accordance with an earlier order. "Had the petitioner [SpiceJet] deposited ₹50 crores, this Court could have entertained the plea of depositing the document of property in Gurgaon as security for permitting the amount of ₹94 crores. However, as the petitioner has not deposited ₹50 crores as per his undertaking, I am not inclined to accept the property as security. Application dismissed," the bench said. Justice Kumar stated that had the deposit of ₹50 crores been made by SpiceJet, the Court would have taken a lenient decision for the second installment. "This Court could have taken a lenient in respect of time limit of second installment, had the petitioner complied with their own undertaking to deposit ₹50 crores with Registrar General in 45 days. Even this part of undertaking has not been complied with," the bench said. Thus, the Court rejected SpiceJet's application seeking extension of time to deposit the money. items.title: Cars torched, vehicles attacked as YSRCP-TDP clashes erupt during local body nominations
items.summary: Violent clashes took place between the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) during the nominations for the Local Body elections on Friday, October 16, with vehicles vandalised, cars set on fire and several people injured. Both the parties blamed each other for attacking party candidates. YSRCP MP PV Midhun Reddy’s convoy was attacked with stones, sticks, and iron rods, allegedly by TDP workers, while he was accompanying his party candidates to file nominations in Punganur town of Annamayya district on Friday, October 16. Videos showed groups of people throwing stones and sticks at passing cars. The YSRCP alleged that TDP leaders and workers blocked MP P V Midhun Reddy’s convoy as it headed to the nomination centre at Basavaraja Government Junior College, then attacked the vehicles and vandalised those belonging to YSRCP leaders. TDP leaders have in turn alleged that it was Midhun Reddy’s supporters and YSRCP cadres who attacked them. Madhusudhan Naidu, TDP’s Punganur in-charge, alleged that YSRCP workers threw glass bottles at TDP leaders who were filing their nominations, and tried to hit them with their cars. Visuals showed MP Midhun Reddy’s gunmen were also injured during the clashes at the Punganur nomination centre. Several vehicles were set on fire in Rayachoti amid the tensions on the first day of filing nominations for the upcoming local body elections. The party has also alleged incidents of intimidation, death threats and obstruction of YSRCP candidates in Tadipatri, Tirupati, Kadapa, and Rayachoti. In a letter to the State Election Commissioner (SEC), YSRCP state general secretary Lella Appi Reddy also alleged that police present at the location remained spectators instead of intervening to stop the violence. The party demanded that the State Election Commission intervene and direct the police to register criminal cases and arrest those responsible, and take action against officers who failed to prevent the attack. It also sought protection for candidates to file their nominations safely. YSRCP MP Maddila Gurumoorthy also wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, seeking their intervention in the attack on Rajampet MP Midhun Reddy, who is also the YSRCP’s floor leader in the Lok Sabha. Midhun Reddy’s father and former state Minister Peddireddy Ramachandra Reddy said the TDP government and the police must take responsibility for the attack on the MP.

items.summary: After 10 days in hospital, most of them in the intensive care unit (ICU), Sona*, a 20-year-old Dalit woman and the survivor in the Kalamassery gang rape case, was discharged on Tuesday, October 13. “She is better now, she has started talking,” said her husband, who was with her at the Kalamassery Medical College in Kochi. Sona’s nightmare started on October 2 when she attended an interview for the position of manager at a private Ayurvedic spa in Edappally, dreaming of a job after she took a break due to an abortion. She got the job, after which she was invited to attend an office party in the evening at a hotel nearby. There she was sexually assaulted by at least three men and one woman for almost two days after allegedly being given narcotic substances. After managing to escape from the hotel, she opened up about the incident to her husband and they subsequently filed a police complaint. “We decided to complain because we don’t want any other woman to go through the same experience. We will continue our legal fight. Someone needs to fight them. If something like this happens, no one speaks about it; that’s what they also want. But this should end,” Sona’s husband told TNM. Two days after the alleged crime, the Kalamassery police arrested two accused – 30-year-old Sreeraj from Alappuzha and 27-year-old Jith Martin from Ernakulam. Both were remanded to judicial custody. On October 7, the police arrested two more accused, Saranya (Ammu) and VS Sanjay, who were absconding after the incident. Investigation is under way to check if there are any more victims. Police also found that the key accused, Sreeraj, is a habitual offender and has been booked in similar cases earlier. Meanwhile, a severely injured Sona was admitted to the Kalamassery Medical College’s ICU. Her husband recalled that she remained silent throughout the first few days of her hospitalisation, and later got better and identified the attackers. items.summary: The Supreme Court of India, on Thursday, October 15, ruled that a Scheduled Caste or Backward Class individual who converts from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu religion such as Islam or Christianity cannot claim affirmative action or reservation benefits based solely on their pre-conversion status. A bench comprising Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar delivered the ruling while dismissing a Special Leave Petition preferred by the Tamil Nadu government against a Madras High Court judgement. The bench ordered, "A person who converts to Islam by that act alone doesn't become a member of one of the seven notified backward class social communities in the state. His former caste status can't be transposed to the Muslim backward class category, nor can his private religious body conclusively determine such status entitlement." The top court's decision affirms the quashing of Tamil Nadu Government Order GO (Ms) No 314 issued on March 9, 2024. The order had allowed individuals converting to Islam from Backward Classes (BC), Most Backward Classes (MBC), Denotified Communities (DNC), or Scheduled Castes (SC) to be issued community certificates under one of the seven notified Backward Class Muslim sects to avail a 3.5% statutory reservation. The seven notified sects under the Tamil Nadu Act 45 of 1994 are Ansar, Dekkani Muslims, Dudekula, Labbais (including Rowthar and Marakayar), Mapilla, Sheik, and Syed. The legal battle originated from a plea filed by Sameer Ahamed (originally named Paramasivara), who converted from Hinduism to Islam in September 2015. A gazette notification was issued in November 2016, and he subsequently married according to Islamic customs. However, when Ahamed applied for a Backward Class (Muslim) community certificate as a "Muslim Labbai", the Kayathar Taluk Office rejected his application on November 13, 2020, stating he had "only converted to religion and not to the caste." items.title: Delhi BJP MLA-led Ramlila committee to burn giant cockroach effigy for Dussehra
items.summary: As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) continues to protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee has decided to burn a 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy alongside those of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations in Delhi, giving the event a political colour. BJP’s Model Town MLA Ashok Goel Devaraha, who is also the president of the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee, claimed that the decision was taken to highlight the need to “eliminate filth from homes, neighbourhoods and society at large.” “The festival of Vijayadashami is celebrated with great enthusiasm across the entire country. It symbolises the triumph of truth over falsehood, good over evil, and righteousness (dharma) over unrighteousness (adharma). For thousands of years, we have been burning the effigies of Ravana, Meghnada, and Kumbhakarna; this conveys the message that, in the end, truth always prevails, “ Devaraha told news agency ANI. Talking about the decision to burn a cockroach effigy, he said the committee had followed the practice in previous years to highlight issues affecting the country. “Keeping these principles in mind, we have also, in the past, burned effigies representing various afflictions plaguing our nation, such as Naxalism or terrorism. This year, our committee has decided to burn an effigy of a cockroach, a symbol of filth, at the Keshav Ramlila Committee grounds (NSP). Our goal is to eliminate filth from three areas: our homes, our immediate surroundings, and society at large,” he said. He added that the effigy would be set alight at the committee's grounds in Pitampura. The CJP is demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over massive irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls which have resulted in the disenfranchisement of crores of eligible voters from the rolls. The Election Commission and the BJP, however, deny allegations of voter manipulation. Two of CJP’s leaders—Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka—are currently under arrest for entering Jantar Mantar grounds against the court’s orders.

items.title: TN minister P Venkataraman defends remark linking rice to social status
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Food and Civil Supplies Minister P Venkataraman on Friday, October 16, defended his controversial remarks linking urban consumers’ preference for premium rice varieties to social status. His comments were made in the backdrop of criticism against the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) led government over rising rice prices. Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat on October 15, the minister had said that consumers in urban areas preferred Karnataka Ponni and Andhra Ponni rice partly because of their social standing ( samuga anthasthu ), rather than necessity. He attributed the increase in prices to limited supplies of these varieties, maintaining that rice cultivated in Tamil Nadu continued to be available at normal rates. In an attempt to clarify his statement a day later on October 16, Venkataraman said his reference to social status was intended to explain the consumption patterns of urban residents. He also stressed on his supposed familiarity with the challenges faced by ordinary consumers, saying he had consumed ration rice since birth. The minister blamed hoarding by certain political leaders and rice mill owners allegedly associated with political parties for contributing to the shortage of premium rice varieties and the subsequent price rise. He called for the current increase in rice prices to be assessed against data from the past five years. According to Venkataraman, around 90% of people in rural areas purchase commodities using ration cards, while the impact of rising prices is more evident in urban centres. He said district-level committees had been established to curb hoarding and assured consumers that palm oil distribution was proceeding smoothly. The minister added that fine varieties of Ponni rice grown in Tamil Nadu were being sold at Rs 60 per kg through cooperative supermarkets. items.title: ED issues summons to former Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan in CMRL-Exalogic case
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has issued summons to former Kerala chief minister and leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) - Exalogic payoff case to appear at the ED’s Kochi office on October 23. The ED’s move came hours after Pinarayi filed an appeal on Friday, October 16, against the Kerala High Court’s direction to the state Vigilance to register a first information report (FIR) in the CMRL case. The state Vigilance department had, on October 12, registered FIRs against Pinarayi, his daughter T Veena and son-in-law PA Mohammed Riyas based on the report filed by the ED under section 66 (2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Following this, the ED registered Enforcement Case Information Reports (ECIR) against Pinarayi and Riyas. When the appeal was filed in the Supreme Court on Friday, senior advocate Siddharth Luthra had requested for an urgent hearing, while informing the court that the 82-year-old former CM might be taken into custody. Considering the plea, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that he can try to list the appeal before a special vacation bench, subject to the availability of judges. Along with Pinarayi, Veena and Riyas too filed appeals in the SC. The ED had conducted raids in connection with the CMRL case at Pinarayi’s residences in Thiruvananthapuram and Kannur on May 27. The raid had triggered a massive protest by CPI(M) members, which ended in an attack on ED officials’ car in Thiruvananthapuram. Over a dozen CPI(M) workers were arrested over the violence. After the raid, the ED claimed to have collected handwritten notes belonging to Veena, which showed suspicious transactions of amounts to the United Arab Emirates through companions of her husband and MLA Riyas. According to the ED, the payments received by Veena and her now defunct IT firm were payoffs to Pinarayi. Around Rs 3.28 crore was paid to Exalogic Solutions and Veena between 2017 and 2020. The ED report said that neither Veena nor her firm has provided any consultancy or software-related services to CMRL.
